rumors: Nobody will say where the mealwood went.
That's why we don't talk about sublevel 4 anymore.
Apparently it wasn't even a real inspection.
Last time this happened they just sealed the room and moved on.
Don't tell anyone I told you that.
Everyone agreed not to mention it in the meeting and somehow that made it worse.
I counted. There were seven. Now there are nine. Nobody brought two more.
I heard it came from inside the base.
It wasn't there yesterday. I'm just saying.
I'm not saying it followed me. I'm saying it was there, and then it was also there.
It was definitely haunted before the renovation.
Nobody admitted it but we all saw the numbers.
Nobody told the new one about the east corridor and now it's too late.
Someone filed a report. Nobody knows who.
Someone keeps moving the mop. Every cycle. Same mop. Different spot.
That's the third time this cycle.
The door was locked from the inside. We checked.
The new one doesn't blink enough.
There's a dent in the wall that wasn't there before and nobody is claiming responsibility.
They said it was a maintenance issue. It was not a maintenance issue.
Two people asked me about it today. Neither of them knows the other asked.
We don't ask about that room anymore.
We think it started before the last printer cycle but nobody kept records.
Whoever wrote that on the storage bin, we know it was you, and we have questions.
Word is management already knows and decided not to tell anyone.
You know how sometimes you feel like you're being observed? Yeah.
The timing is suspicious. That's all I'm saying.
Apparently someone requested a transfer to sublevel 6. Nobody has been to sublevel 6.
I'm not saying it's related. I'm just saying they happened on the same cycle.
It was fine this morning. It is not fine now.
small_talk: Anyway, I'm not worried about it.
That's a tomorrow problem.
Honestly the worst part is how good I've gotten at pretending everything is fine.
I asked for a different bunk assignment four cycles ago. Still pending.
I ate eight rations and I still wake up thinking about food.
I don't think about the void below us. I just don't.
I keep having this dream where the base has windows. Real ones.
I named mine Gerald. I know. I know.
I've been awake so long I started making friends with the sweep bot. He's consistent.
I've been shoveling for six cycles and I'm going to say it: I'm good at it.
I've done worse for fewer calories.
I've started rating the ladders. The one by sector 3 is a solid seven.
I'm not saying it's cursed. I'm saying I wouldn't touch it.
I'm not tired. I'm just conserving energy.
It's only excessive if it negatively impacts productivity. It doesn't. Probably.
Sometimes I just stand in the oxygen room to confirm the oxygen.
My stress level is technically fine. Technically.
That smell has always been there.
Nobody complimented the pipe routing and I worked hard on that pipe routing.
One day I'm going to build a room just for standing in. No tasks. Just standing.
She named it. You can't butcher something that has a name.
Eight rations. Don't judge me.
Technically that's still within acceptable parameters.
The atmo suit makes me feel powerful. I've said what I said.
The hum from the generator is different now and I'm choosing not to investigate that.
The schedule says rest period. The rest period is theoretical.
The slimelung comes and goes. It's part of life.
We've been out of snacks for six cycles. I'm adapting.
I drew it myself. It helps.
You get used to the noise eventually.
observations: It's been making that sound for two cycles now.
The atmo suit queue is twelve deep every morning. At some point that's a design problem.
Battery reserves are down again. Same amount. Same cycle. Every time.
The biome scanner is picking up a signature that doesn't match any known critter.
Generator output is suspiciously stable. I don't trust stable.
That pipe was definitely not there before.
I filed the incident report. The incident report is now also an incident.
I logged it. Nobody responded to the log.
It's growing. I don't know what it is but it's growing.
Just keep an eye on it. That's all I'm saying.
Nobody knows where the power is going.
The polluted oxygen pocket grew another eight tiles. I'm keeping an eye on it.
The power grid tripped twice. Third time and I start filling out the forms.
There's a puddle near the electrolyzers. I'm calling it decorative until someone tells me otherwise.
Something moved in the lower biome. Could be nothing.
That generator has been at ninety-eight percent for too long.
The auto-sweeper is ignoring everything except that one tile.
The farm tiles are producing something. I'm not sure it's food.
The morb population doubled while I was on rest period. I don't know how.
The oxygen is fine. The oxygen has always been fine. Stop asking.
The pip was in the food hall again. Same spot. Same plant. Same expression.
The plumbing in sector 3 started making a new noise. It replaced the old noise. I miss the old noise.
The pump hasn't stopped running in thirty cycles. The pipe is fine. Allegedly.
The readings are normal. The readings are always normal right before.
The transit tube has been backing up since cycle forty and nobody will commit to fixing it.
There's a heat signature in the east wall that wasn't there before.
There are more of them than there were yesterday.
Three stress vomits in one cycle. I'm logging it as a morale event.
Two farm tiles. Zero yield. Investigating.
Whatever it is, it's warm.
party_phone: No no no listen, listen — I know what I saw. It was not a morb. Morbs don't do that. I've worked near morbs for six cycles and they have never once done that, okay, so whatever that thing was, it was not a morb, and I need you to take that seriously.

So here's the thing. Here's the thing. The schedule says I'm on rest period, right, but the errand board says I'm supposed to be digging out sector 7, and both of those things cannot be true at the same time, and yet somehow nobody else thinks this is a problem worth solving.

I'm not saying management is wrong. I would never say that on this line. I'm saying that there's a version of the situation where someone with more information might look at the same facts and reach a different conclusion, and I think you're smart enough to know what I mean by that.

Okay so the pipe burst was my fault. Technically. But in my defense, the blueprint said that valve was closed, and I had no reason to believe the blueprint was aspirational rather than descriptive, so I think morally it's not entirely on me.

I've been awake for two cycles running and I'm starting to see tiles that aren't there. Not scary ones. Just, like, extra tiles. Bonus tiles. But I wanted to tell someone in case it gets worse and I stop being able to tell the difference between the bonus tiles and the real ones.

She named it. I know, I know, I know — you're not supposed to name them. But she named it Biscuit and now it follows her to the food hall and I don't know how to log that in the incident report, like what category is that even, is that morale, is that a critter containment issue, help.

The thing about the oxygen is that it's fine right now. Right now it's fine. But I've been doing the math in my head for three days and if you run the numbers at current consumption rates with current production levels then there's a window — a small window — a window I'm not going to describe out loud on this line — but it's there.

Okay you have to promise not to tell anyone. Promise? Okay. Someone has been reorganizing the storage bins at night. Nobody knows who. The bins are actually more organized than before. We're all scared.

I don't know how to explain this without sounding like I've lost it, but the sweeper bot has been sweeping the same tile for four cycles. Just that tile. Nothing else. I put a different item near it and it ignored the item. It just keeps sweeping. The tile is clean. The tile has been clean for days. I don't know what it sees.

My assigned bunk is next to the generator. Which is fine. I like the hum. The hum is consistent. Predictable. What is not consistent or predictable is the new sound the generator started making on cycle forty-seven, which is different from the hum, and which I have now heard in my sleep twice, and I just needed to tell someone that.

She said it was a shortcut. And look — it got us there faster. I'll give her that. But there is a corridor in sector 9 that did not exist before she found the shortcut, and I think we need to ask some questions about where that corridor came from and whether we're okay with it being there.

I put in a request for a window. Six cycles ago. The request is still listed as pending. I've checked. I check every day. It's still pending. I don't need the window anymore. I drew one on the wall and honestly I think it looks better than a real one would. But I want to know what pending means. What does it mean. Nobody will tell me what it means.

Okay so you know how the farm tiles near sublevel 2 have been underperforming? And everyone said it was just a nutrient thing, soil rotation, totally normal? I pulled the actual logs. It's not a nutrient thing. I don't know what it is. It started on the same cycle the new duplicant arrived and I am not saying those things are connected. I'm just saying they're adjacent.

The morale score went up by four points last cycle and I've been trying to figure out why because nothing changed. Nothing visibly changed. And then I realized the only thing that happened was that someone moved the plant near the mess hall approximately six inches to the left. Six inches. Four morale. I've been staring at that plant for an hour.

I know it's just a critter. I know that. But it looked at me. Like, at me specifically. And then it turned around and walked the other direction and I just — I don't know. It knew something. I don't know what it knew but it knew something and it decided I wasn't worth telling.

I'm not having a breakdown. I want to be really clear about that. What I'm having is an extended moment of reassessment that happens to involve me sitting on the floor of the supply room for the past forty minutes, and I called you because you're the only person who wouldn't immediately escalate that to a wellness check, so please just talk to me about literally anything else.

I ran the numbers. I know I always say that and then something goes wrong but this time I actually ran them and wrote them down and checked them twice, and the water situation is fine, but only if we stop doing the thing we're currently doing with the water, and I can't get anyone to stop doing the thing, so the numbers are fine in theory only.

She put in a priority override on her own errands. Did you know you could do that? I didn't know you could do that. I've been doing work in the order it was assigned like some kind of rule-follower, and apparently there's a checkbox, just a checkbox, and she found it, and now she only digs near the coffee machine and honestly I respect it but I'm also furious.

I need to say this fast before my shift starts. You know the locked room on sublevel 3? The one nobody talks about? I found a key. I don't know whose key it is. It was in my pocket when I woke up. I didn't put it there. I'm going to put it back somewhere and pretend I never found it and I need you to confirm that this is the correct decision.

The food is fine. I'm not complaining about the food. I'm just saying that bristle berry mush and bristle berry mush and bristle berry mush is technically three different meals and only one of them should be called mush and the other two deserve better names, and I've been thinking about this for eleven cycles and I needed to say it out loud to another person.

Okay so I have to tell you what happened with the drecko because I still can't process it alone. I was doing the routine sweep of the ranch, normal cycle, nothing unusual, and I counted the dreckos and there were four, which is correct, four is the right number, except one of them was wearing what I can only describe as a hat. Not a hat we gave it. A hat it found. Or made. I don't know which is worse.

The schedule has me assigned to three different locations at the same time on cycle fifty-two and I know it's a clerical error and I know I should just pick one and move on but I've been standing here for twenty minutes trying to decide which task a reasonable person would prioritize and I genuinely cannot and I needed to hear another voice before I made a decision I'd regret.

I don't want to alarm you but I've been tracking the idle time logs and there's a duplicant who has been listed as idle for eleven cycles straight and nobody has assigned them anything and when I walk past them they're just standing in the corridor near the water cooler and they nod at me when I go by and I nod back and it's been eleven cycles and I don't know how to ask.

You know what I think about? Soil. I think about the soil. Not in a concerning way. In a genuinely curious way. Like, we brought seeds. We built the farm tiles. We set up the irrigation. But where did the soil come from. Nobody packed soil. I've asked three people. None of them had an answer. I'm going to keep asking. I need to know where the soil came from.

I submitted a formal suggestion to add a second ladder in the east wing and I thought that would be the end of it, just a suggestion in the box, but apparently it triggered a review process, and the review process triggered a committee, and the committee wants a presentation, and now I have to do a presentation about a ladder, and I've been preparing for six cycles and I'm still not ready.
